prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder circuits within approved limits; observation never substitutes for protection/control/field verification.
Bay Automation Controller (Juniper), comprising North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller, sequences/interlocks bays, produces Bay Status Digest, timestamps local changes. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized interlocked commands; local authority prevails; remote operation requires station authority/selection/availability/permitted modes. Station Gateway carries authorized remote communications.
Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects feeders using approved settings; produces Relay Diagnostic Note for fault analysis by Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur), who compares event times/relay indications and documents uniquely revisioned, coordinated study-based changes. Independent review/approval, compatibility, installation comparison/functional checks precede deployment; discrepancies block release.
Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) presents current indications/quality separately from archived evidence, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; communications loss invalidates currency; recovery requires verification.
Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) distributes reference time, produces Clock Drift Snapshot; loss invokes holdover, affects interpretation without discarding evidence. Quality: synchronized/degraded/unavailable; timestamps cannot establish measurement/protection validity.
Station DC System powers protection/automation; produces Battery Load Test Record for engineering retention.
Sequence Event Archive (Orchard) preserves original ordering, source/event/receipt times/quality, flags uncertainty, distinguishes corrected/estimated times, retains administration/configuration/access history. Authorized access; auditable changes; scheduled/utility retention; investigation holds require responsible release; health checks capacity/ingestion/recoverability; restoration preserves readability/timestamps/quality; protected backup required.
Engineering Workstation produces Settings Review Receipt, controls revisions/history, provides approved search/filter/export; queries should bound station/equipment/time. Exports preserve timestamps/flags; derived ordering/conclusions remain separate interpretations.
Maintenance Remote Terminal permits authorized maintenance. Substation Supervisor enforces suitability/authorization.
Substation Field Crew (Cinder) verifies hazards/isolation/identity locally, sends Breaker Inspection Tag(condition/time); uncertainty/discrepancies require hold/escalation; completion accounts personnel/tools/connections.
Control Room Operator verifies states/reviews sequences, submits equipment/change/timing requests.
Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) maintains station-wide plan, coordinates bays, checks clearance/work conflicts, confirms handback; work evidence remains reviewable.

Document units:
S127: The Substation Supervisor resolves priority conflicts and confirms the operational authority for exceptional switching conditions.
S128: Approved switching sequences identify the required order of actions, hold points, and conditions for stopping work.
S129: The North Bay Controller manages control and interlocking functions assigned to the north bay under the approved sequence.
S130: The North Bay Controller blocks a close command when its local interlocks indicate that the bay is not ready.
S131: The South Bay Controller manages the corresponding control and interlocking functions assigned to the south bay.
S132: The two controllers have separate equipment scopes and do not substitute for one another when executing a switching sequence.
S133: The bay boundary defines which controller may operate each device and which indications are used to confirm its state.
S134: Equipment shared across the boundary requires explicit coordination before a switching action can affect either bay.
S135: The Bay Automation Controller presents bay control status while preserving the separate operating scopes of the two controllers.
S136: The Breaker Control Unit executes permitted breaker commands only when the applicable control conditions are satisfied.
S137: The North Protection Panel supports protection functions for the north-side equipment within its assigned scope.
S138: The Transformer Protection Panel retains its protection authority independently of the bay switching sequence.
S139: The Station Supervisory Control System uses the status digest to review current station operating conditions.
S140: The Sequence Event Archive receives the Clock Drift Snapshot for event-time correlation.
S141: The Switching Desk Coordinator produces the Isolation Boundary Card for the planned work.
S142: The Station Gateway produces the Protocol Retry Summary for communication review.
S143: Larkspur reviews protection coordination questions that could affect the planned switching sequence.
S144: Bluefin provides the station time reference used to align recorded event times.
S145: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S146: After the Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback, state-change evidence remains available for authorized engineering review.
S147: Alarm indications are assessed according to protection significance, equipment condition, and the potential effect on service.
S148: The Control Room Operator reviews the alarm priority, source, time, and associated bay indications before deciding on a response.
S149: The operator distinguishes a new alarm from a standing condition and checks whether related indications support the same assessment.
S150: For a protection operation or an unexplained equipment state, the Control Room Operator treats the condition as requiring prompt investigation.
